issue: The inline annotation reads '8× savings vs GQA FP16 (2.62 → 0.33 MB/tok)', which names GQA FP16 as the comparison baseline. The arrow and the numbers show the reduction is from full-MHA FP16 (2.62 MB/tok) to GQA FP16 (0.33 MB/tok); GQA is the smaller value, not the baseline being reduced.
evidence: Annotation in Figure 7.5: '8× savings vs GQA FP16 (2.62 → 0.33 MB/tok)'; legend identifies 2.62 MB/tok as full-MHA FP16 and 0.33 MB/tok as GQA FP16; caption says 'GQA with a 64:8 query-to-KV head ratio ~8× smaller.'
acceptance_test: Annotation names the correct baseline and direction, e.g. 'GQA FP16: 8× smaller than full-MHA FP16 (2.62 → 0.33 MB/tok)' or '8× savings vs full-MHA FP16'.

issue: The inline annotations ('9.5K max context ...', '8× savings ...', '~436 GB budget at 166K') are set noticeably smaller than the axis/legend text and are difficult to read at print size; the dense annotation text also competes with the plotted lines.
evidence: At 150 dpi the annotation glyphs are visibly smaller than the axis tick labels and legend; the '8× savings...' line is a long string placed inside the plot area.
acceptance_test: All figure annotations measure at least 8 pt at print size, or the detail is moved into the caption/legend with only short leader labels left in the plot.

issue: The figure states 'No compatible kernel: reject; fallback is not guaranteed.' The caption says 'Unsupported combinations may be rejected; fallback is not guaranteed.' The figure's unqualified 'reject' is stronger than the caption and can be read as a universal guarantee of rejection, whereas some runtimes may fall back to a slower path or fail differently.
evidence: Figure text: 'No compatible kernel: reject; fallback is not guaranteed.' Caption: 'Unsupported combinations may be rejected; fallback is not guaranteed.'
acceptance_test: Figure text matches the caption's modality, e.g. 'No compatible kernel: may reject; fallback is not guaranteed' or 'cannot execute without a compatible kernel'.

issue: The arrows from 'Error-control method' and 'Numerical representation' terminate on the outer 'Container wraps tensors + metadata' box rather than on the 'Packed tensor' box. This blurs the distinction the caption draws between the packed tensor and the checkpoint container.
evidence: In Figure 7.3 the two top boxes' downward arrows enter the top edge of the large container box; the 'Packed tensor: values + scales...' box sits inside that container and receives no arrow.
acceptance_test: Arrows terminate on the packed-tensor box, or the container is clearly drawn as a downstream wrapper after packing.

issue: The 'sample p99' label is placed at the top left of the plot, far from the red dashed 1.33 s line it names, and has no leader. A reader can momentarily associate the label with the nearby p50/p90/p95 cluster instead of the 1.33 s line.
evidence: In Figure 6.2 the red 'sample p99' text sits above the green p50 label near x≈0.8, while the red dashed sample-p99 line is at x≈1.33; the boxed note 'sample p99 (interpolation) = 1.33s' is the only direct tie.
acceptance_test: The 'sample p99' label is adjacent to the 1.33 s line or connected by a leader; no ambiguity remains at print size.

issue: The bar fills use hatching on the inference and QLoRA bars but a solid fill on the full fine-tune bar, with no legend or caption explaining what the pattern encodes. This is a gratuitous visual distinction that can imply a semantic difference where none is stated.
evidence: Figure 7.6: inference bar is blue with diagonal hatching; QLoRA bar is green with diagonal hatching; full fine-tune bar is solid red. The caption and in-figure notes describe only the quantities, not the fill patterns.
acceptance_test: Either the hatching encodes a stated distinction (and is explained in the caption/legend), or all bars use a consistent fill treatment.
